title: Predictor variables for a 100-km race time in male ultra-marathoners
authors: Knechtle B, Knechtle P, Rosemann T, Senn O
findings: Bivariate correlations with 100-km race time: mean weekly running km r = -.43, mean training speed r = -.56, mean weekly running hours r = -.21, personal best marathon time r = .65, percent body fat r = .45, personal best 100-km time r = .72.
Stepwise regression: training speed, weekly running kilometres and age were the best predictors (all p<.0001); r2 = .43.
Reported equation: 100-km time (min) = 1085.60 - 36.26 x training speed (km/h) - 1.43 x training volume (km/wk) + 2.50 x age (yr).
Authors suggest training intensity may matter more than anthropometry for a successful 100-km outcome.
limitations: Self-reported, male only, cross-sectional, r2 only .43, collinearity of speed with ability; equation not validated here. Author list beyond the first author taken from memory of the paper and not re-checked; only the first author was verified in Crossref.
implications: For 100 km goals include both weekly distance and training speed (and marathon PB) as predictors; do not assume volume alone drives ultra performance.
Do not use the equation for individual prescription; it is a population association with r2 .43.
